subject: Geography
source_policy: Configured official GSET syllabus headings and available question stems/options. Original source-page visual sign-off is not claimed where the scan was not available.

records.question_summary: Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico are adjacent to which ocean?
records.rationale: Ocean-basin adjacency is most closely aligned with oceanography; Unit III covers ocean relief and oceanographic geography. Candidate only because exact ocean-location topic is not named verbatim in the syllabus.

records.question_summary: One-third land of which country has been reclaimed from the sea?
records.rationale: Land reclamation is not explicitly named in any of the ten unit descriptions. No defensible single-unit assignment; retain unassigned pending subject-expert decision.

records.question_summary: Question matches social/cultural concepts such as information society, cultural capital and post-industrial society.
records.rationale: These are social and cultural geography concepts and align most closely with Unit VII social structure/processes and cultural geography. OCR author-pair wording still requires source-page review.

records.question_summary: Question matches tribes and habitats.
records.rationale: Tribal/cultural groups and their spatial distribution align most closely with Unit VII social geography; syllabus wording specifically mentions spatial distribution of social groups in India, so world-region scope remains a limitation.

records.question_summary: A tombolo is a coastal depositional landform connecting an island to another island or mainland.
records.rationale: The object asked is a landform and is best placed under Unit I landform occurrence and geomorphic processes; Unit III coastal waves may be related but is not the primary concept.

records.question_summary: Question asks the author of Geography of Towns.
records.rationale: Urban and settlement geography is explicitly covered in Unit V; the prior Unit VIII Geographic Thought proposal was a weaker fit.

records.question_summary: Clark and Evans are associated with the nearest-neighbour method.
records.rationale: Nearest-neighbour analysis is a spatial statistical technique; Unit IX explicitly covers spatial data, sampling, cluster analysis and related quantitative techniques.

records.question_summary: Question matches world islands with the oceans in which they are located.
records.rationale: Ocean-basin identification is most closely aligned with Unit III Oceanography, although world-island location is not explicitly named.

records.question_summary: Question matches Indian national parks with their locations.
records.rationale: The question is specifically about locations within India and is closest to Unit X Geography of India; Unit IV ecosystem content is related but the tested task is Indian regional location.

records.question_summary: Question compares colluvial, aeolian, alluvial and glacial soil/material characteristics.
records.rationale: The distinctions concern transported surface materials and geomorphic agents, making Unit I the closest available fit. Soil taxonomy itself is not explicitly listed, so retain provisional status.

records.question_summary: Question compares racial/ethnic group classifications.
records.rationale: This is closest to Unit VII cultural and social geography and its coverage of social groups; exact historical classification wording must be source-checked.

records.question_summary: Question asks rock types occurring in Kutch and north-eastern Kathiawar.
records.rationale: The syllabus does not explicitly list regional lithology or geological periods. Unit I and Unit X are both arguable but neither is sufficiently direct; retain unassigned pending expert decision.

records.question_summary: Question asks soil colour under hot-dry climate in climatogenic soil classification.
records.rationale: The question combines soil classification and climate, but soil taxonomy is not explicit in the unit descriptions. Do not force Unit II; retain unassigned pending expert decision.

records.question_summary: Vegetation type is identified from rainfall, temperature, humidity and evergreen character.
records.rationale: Natural vegetation/ecosystems are the closest fit to Unit IV ecosystem and human ecology; Unit X natural resources is a secondary possible fit.

records.question_summary: Podsol soil in coniferous biome and cold humid climate.
records.rationale: Soil/biome/ecosystem connection suggests Unit IV as a tentative candidate, but soil types are not explicit in the syllabus. Keep pending for expert approval.

records.question_summary: Rock types in Kutch and north-eastern Kathiawar.
records.rationale: Same unresolved lithology issue as November 2023 Q1. No direct syllabus unit; retain pending.

records.question_summary: Question asks which oasis is not correctly matched.
records.rationale: Oasis is a landform/geomorphic environment candidate for Unit I, but options and exact matching context must be reviewed before assigning.

records.question_summary: Lithosphere statements; OCR/source transcription hold.
records.rationale: Exact option wording is unresolved. No mapping decision until the official printed question page is inspected.

records.question_summary: Life cycle of a renewable energy source.
records.proposed_unit_name: Geography of Economic Activities and Regional Development
records.rationale: Energy resources and energy crises are explicit Unit VI themes; provisional Unit VI candidate, subject to full stem/options review.

records.question_summary: Matching question combines primate city/megalopolis/rank-size (Unit V) with growth pole (Unit VI).
records.rationale: The stem spans two units; do not force a single-unit mapping. Retain pending or use a multi-unit model only if the app schema supports it.

records.question_summary: Arrange geological periods from recent to oldest.
records.rationale: Geological-period chronology is not explicitly listed in the ten syllabus unit descriptions. Retain pending expert decision.

note: Model-supported syllabus adjudication proposals only; not a named human subject expert's approval. All cases remain review-only.
